newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-The Weekend in Australian Sport.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-The Weekend in Australian Sport.

text.p: CRICKET
SYDNEY - Australia leg-spinner Shane Warne gave a career-best limited overs performance as Australia humbled West Indies by eight wickets on Sunday to take a 2-0 lead in the World Series competition.
Warne was twice on a hat trick as West Indies lost their last six wickets for 19 runs in the space of 37 deliveries to be all out for 161 in 48.3 overs.
Australia reached their target after losing two wickets, opening batsman Mark Waugh steering Australia home with an unbeaten 83 with eight overs to spare.
Ricky Ponting was bowled by West Indies captain Courtney Walsh for 44 after a 98 run partnership with Waugh.
Warne had earlier torn through the West Indian tail, taking five wickets at a cost of just five runs.
His match figures of five for 33 were his best in 61 matches and bettered his previous best of four for 19 against New Zealand three years ago.

Warne dismissed middle order batsman Roland Holder and fast bowler Nixon McLean in successive deliveries and then repeated the feat in his next over to remove wicketkeeper Junior Murray and pace bowler Kenneth Benjamin.
World record holding batsman Brian Lara was again disappointing for West Indies. His inings of 26 brought his tally in his last four innings to a meagre 34.

Australia now lead West Indies 2-0 after a five-wicket win on Friday night. Pakistan were due to arrive in Australia on Tuesday and will play the Australian Cricket Academy on Friday ahead of their first World Series match against Australia in Adelaide on Sunday.
RUGBY UNION

LONDON - David Campese scored the final try of his long and illustrious international career as Australia completed their unbeaten tour of Europe with a 39-12 thrashing of the Barbarians at Twickenham on Saturday.
Fullback Matt Burke scored 24 points from two tries, two penalties and four conversions in a peerless performance but it was winger Campese who stole the show.
Campese celebrated the end of his 14-year career with a try in the 48th minute, one of five scored by Australia.
He later received a standing ovation from an appreciative crowd of 65,000 as he jogged around the field ahead of his team-mates.
"Today was a great game to finish with. Everyone enjoyed it and I think that's what rugby's all about," Campese said.

"Scoring a try doesn't really matter. What I've done over the years is great, but there are other great players out there. If you can be a part of it and throw a good pass that's just as good as scoring a try."
The 34-year-old had played 101 tests and scored a world record 64 test tries in an often controversial career for the Wallabies.
The Barbarians fielded 14 internationals but were out of the game by halftime as Australia served up some tasty rugby before taking their foot off the gas in the final quarter.

The result saw Australia finish unbeaten from 12 matches on tour, including tests against Italy, Ireland, Scotland and Wales. Despite that record coach Greg Smith had endured constant criticism during the tour for the occasionally unconvincing displays by his side.
Campese later said he would consider playing club rugby in England but thought business opportunities in Australia would prevent him from joining rich clubs such as Saracens.
"If the opportunity is there I'd obviously think about it but the thing that holds me back is business," he said.
"I'd like to come over but there are a lot of things happening at home. I've also got a contract to play for New South Wales in the Super 12 next year."
CRICKET
HOBART - Bellerive Oval proved to be a batsman's paradise as Tasmania reached 161 without loss in their second innings on the third day of their Sheffield Shield match against Victoria on Sunday.
Tasmania led by 211 runs after opener Jamie Cox slammed 102 not out, bringing his century up off 132 deliveries and including 14 boundaries.
Cox's opening partner Dene Hills will resume on 54 not out on the final day as Tasmania seek more quick runs ahead of an expected declaration early on Monday.
Cox became the fifth batsman to score a century in the match, with Tasmanian team-mates David Boon, Michael DiVenuto and Shaun Young all scoring hundreds in their side's first innings.
Former Australia test batsman Dean Jones scored 145 as Victoria reached 431 for nine declared in their first innings, 50 behind Tasmania's first innings of 481 for eight declared.
Tasmania captain Boon later told reporters he hoped to be able to set Victoria a tempting target despite the match being played on a pitch which has so far provided 131 boundaries and four sixes.
"I think our ask has got to be tough, but there's going to be a carrot," he said.
Jones' innings took him past former Australia captain Allan Border as the seventh highest runscorer in Shield cricket.
GOLF
PARAPARAUMU - New Zealand golfer Michael Long held off an army of Australians to win the New Zealand Open by four strokes on Sunday.
Australia's Peter Lonard started the final day at the head of the leaderboard but Long carded a final round of four-under-par 67 for a convincing win in the A$4423,000 tournament.
Second went to defending champion Peter O'Malley on 279, with fellow Australian Shane Tait another shot back in third.
Lonard faltered with a final round 74 to share fourth with compatriots Peter Senior and Paul Barnsley and New Zealand's Greg Turner.
Long took out his national title a week after finishing third behind Senior and world number one Greg Norman in the Greg Norman Classic in Melbourne.
He became the first New Zealander to win his national title since Grant Waite in 1992.
"The pressure was on from last week, everyone knew I was in there and it was just a matter of keeping my emotions in control and doing what I had to do," Long told reporters.

Long took the outright lead with a birdie on the par four 10th hole and added further birdies on the 12th and 16th holes. Lonard faded on the back nine with bogeys on the 13th and 14th and a double bogey on the 17th.
Long took $A78,747 for the biggest win of his career, along with a two-year exemption on the Australasian Tour.
O'Malley came through the field with a closing 66, a fourth round score matched only by Turner.
Lonard's fourth place added to a string of recent top 10 finishes, including seconds at the Singapore Open, the Players Championship and the Australian PGA.
SQUASH
BOMBAY - Scotsman Peter Nicol, described by his Australian opponent Rodney Eyles as having "a heart as big as the cup he won", successfully defended his Mahindra International title on Saturday.
Nicol beat world number two Eyles in a one hour 40 minute final of wildly fluctuating fortunes 13-15 15-10 7-15 17-15 15-13.
Nicol looked a beaten man when he went 10-4 down in the fourth game. But he clawed his way back to lead 14-12 .
Eyles saved three game points before losing the game 17-15 when his forehand volley was adjudged to have passed too close to him and he conceded a penalty stroke.
Eyles was forced to do the scrambling in the deciding game, hauling himself back into contention from 5-1 and then 13-10 down.
But the Australian top seed missed a relatively easy backhand drop shot and then failed to clear the path in the backhand court to give Nicol the match.
World number three Nicol said: "I don't seem to be able to put a foot wrong in Bombay and I hope to come back next year to win the title a third time."
TENNIS

MUNICH - Defending champion Goran Ivanisevic used his record-breaking serve to boost his earnings at the Grand Slam Cup to more than $3.2 million with a 6-4 6-4 quarter-final victory over Australian Mark Woodforde on Friday.

The big-serving Croat, who before this year had earned $2.8 million in four appearances at the most lucrative event in the game, made sure of adding at least another $431,250 to his bank balance with a straightforward win in just 66 minutes.
On the way to his victory, defending champion Ivanisevic took his total of aces for the year to a record of over 1,500.
"Now I can say that I am the best server in the game," Ivanisevic said.
Woodforde added: "I have a lot of respect for that serve because he's able to serve incredibly well. That's probably one of tennis's phenomenons, Goran Ivanisevic's serve."
Asked about his strategy against the Croat, the Australian added. "I think it's obvious. I just try and get the ball back over the net often enough."
Ivanisevic's huge serve is a major asset on the fast indoor surface. It makes it very difficult for his opponents to get on top of his game, as Woodforde found out.

Woodforde had his own serve broken in the third game and Ivanisevic soon had the first set in 31 minutes. Another break in the first game of the second set effectively clinched his place in the semifinals.
The Croat did drop his serve in the eighth game but broke back immediately before finishing off the second set in 33 minutes.
Ivanisevic will face Boris Becker of Germany in the final. Becker beat Tim Henman of Britain 7-6 (7-2) 6-3 while the Croat beat Russia's Yevgeny Kafelnikov 6-7 (6-8) 2-6 6-3 6-2 6-4.
